The main takeaway from our work is that

the synchro-Compton emission in 3C279 is well explained by a shock-in-jet scenario, with the shock wave propagating at a speed of 0.3c, the shock width being about 1/10 of the radius of the emitting region and a magnetic field of 1 G.
the synchroton emission of the blazar jet is highly variable, but the variability is not random and the flaring behaviour is consistent with a simple shock-in-jet scenario.
the shock-in-jets model of blazar variability can explain the observed synchrotron and gamma-ray behaviour of 3C~279.
